texts.preamble: Ravindra Nagappa Markal vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 25 November, 2024 Scch-21 1 Mvc No.5159/2023 Kabc0B0117272023 In The Court Of Xvii Addl. Judge, Court Of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T, Mayo Hall Unit, Bengaluru (Scch-21) Present: Vijaykumar S. Hiremath., L.Lb., Xvii Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T., Bengaluru. Dated this the 25th Day of November-2024 M.V.C. No.5159/2023 Petitioner/s: 1. Sri. Ravindra Nagappa Markal S/o Nagappa Markal, Aged about 33 years, Residing at: Ragihaklu, Patlamane, Shivamogga, Karnataka-577 415. (By Sri. T. Manjunatha, Adv.,) Vs. Respondent/s: 1. M/s Shriram General Insurance Co. Ltd., Motor Claims Hub,
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 13.07.2023. 2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under: It is the case of the petitioner that on 13.07.2023 at about 10.30 p.m., petitioner was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA- 53-HK-4418 slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic rules proceeding near Ramamurthy Nagar Signal, Ramamurthy Nagar, Bangalore, at that time the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. MH-43-BQ-2028 ridden in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of petitioner. Due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body. Immediately, he was shifted to Hosmat Hospital wherein he treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses. The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 33 years, the petitioner was working as Delivery Boy at Swiggy and Zomato and earning Rs.60,000/- per month. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and lost his future income. Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle. Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest. 3. After service of notice, the respondent No.2 remained absent. Hence, placed exparte. The respondent No.1 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent riding of the offending motorcycle. Further, this respondent admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and policy was inforce as on the date of accident and liability if any is subjected to the terms and Ravindra Nagappa Markal vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 25 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87114808/ 2 conditions of the policy. Further, this respondent seeks protection u/s 134, 170 and 149(2) of M. V. Act. The petitioner was not wearing helmet as on the date of accident. He also denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner. The petitioner colluding with the owner and police filed the false case. By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.17 and also examined Dr. Krishan Prasad as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.18 to 23 and closed their side. On the other hand, no evidence is lead on behalf of respondents.
texts.arguments: In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319. 16. Further, learned advocate for insurance company argued that, respondent No.2 has committed offence as per the Motor Vehicles Act, hence insurance company is not liable to pay compensation in the alleged accident. The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses. In support of his plea, he has produced 30 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.14 to the tune of Rs.2,38,396/-. The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,38,396/- towards medical expenses. It is the further contended that, the injured petitioner was working as Delivery boy at Swiggy and Zomato and earning Rs.60,000/- per month, in support of his income he has produced the bank statement. As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.
texts.respondent_arguments: Further, learned advocate for insurance company argued that, respondent No.2 has committed offence as per the Motor Vehicles Act, hence insurance company is not liable to pay compensation in the alleged accident. The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses. In support of his plea, he has produced 30 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.14 to the tune of Rs.2,38,396/-. The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,38,396/- towards medical expenses. It is the further contended that, the injured petitioner was working as Delivery boy at Swiggy and Zomato and earning Rs.60,000/- per month, in support of his income he has produced the bank statement.

No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co.
